idiom_name: Faraday retry middleware with an Idempotency-Key, or stripe-ruby's automatic keys
implementation_notes: Faraday's retry middleware (faraday-retry) retries only idempotent methods by default - delete, get, head, options, put - and accepts an exceptions list, retry_statuses, backoff parameters and a retry_if block, so the loop becomes configuration and opting a POST in is a deliberate act that requires SecureRandom.uuid() as the key. The Stripe Ruby SDK shows the library endpoint of the pattern: Stripe.max_network_retries = 2 and, in its own words, 'idempotency keys are added to requests to guarantee that retries are safe'. The remaining application work is the durable side - persisting the key with the pending operation and, on the receiver, recording key -> outcome.
code_sketch:
require "securerandom"
key = SecureRandom.uuid                     # once per logical operation
conn = Faraday.new(url: base) do |f|
  f.request :retry, max: 3, interval: 0.1, backoff_factor: 2,
                    retry_statuses: [429, 503]
  f.response :raise_error
end
conn.post("/v1/charges") do |req|
  req.headers["Idempotency-Key"] = key      # same key on every replay
  req.body = payload.to_json
end
pitfalls: The middleware's default method list is idempotent-only; adding :post to :methods without a key is how a Faraday client starts double-charging.
The header must be stamped with a key computed outside the request block - Faraday rebuilds the request for each retry, so a SecureRandom.uuid() inside the block is a new operation every time.
retry_if applies only to methods outside :methods unless :methods is emptied, so mixing both options yields either unexpected retries or none at all.
